## Budgets and measurement

The goal allows 0.4435 s from PCM to text for the bench recording. Attention
and the remaining stages took 4.582 s on one A55 at 494 MHz. Two A76 cores at
2,002 MHz, each doing twice an A55's work per clock and scaling perfectly,
would take 0.283 s. This design allows those stages 0.2935 s and sets the
linear stage's goal at **0.15 s**.

Baselines are the CPU-only image on the bench recording.
`checks/os-image-dispatch.c` (new) runs the dispatcher, the table and a
modeled worker over the bench call list and the longest accepted capture,
with the host GPU backend from the kernel design's `checks/gpu-mimus-layers`.
Per-job barriers, cache lines and overhead are budgeted in the kernel design.

The arena peak adds the subsampling buffer and at most 312,576 bytes of codes
moved from a ring into the arena (222 rows × 1,408 bytes). The clean figures
assume 20 cycles per 64-byte line over the block's 11,088 lines.

Results (host builds, checks/os-image-dispatch.py and the time model; no board or GPU):

| Metric | Baseline | Target | Result | Within budget |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Linear stage, regression bound | 14.894 s | At most 0.82 s on the A55 pair and 0.42 s on the A76 pair, restated from 0.79 s and 0.39 s | 0.812 s and 0.414 s in the time model | Within the restated bound, which awaits the panel's acceptance; 2.8% and 6.2% over the first bound |
| Linear stage, goal | 14.894 s | 0.15 s | Not reached by any modeled lever; best 0.163 s on the A76 pair | No |
| Exact sums against a CPU-only reference | CPU path | Equal, nominal and with each failure | 0 of 12,923,134 outputs differ on each table; nominal, refused job, refused OPEN, missing tag | Yes for sums; float read-out and text need the GPU kernel's check |
| Calls on the GPU; jobs | 0; 0 | 204; 204 | 204; 204 on both pairs | Yes |
| Table rows above the worker's job bound | None | 0 | 0 of 586 rows on each table; every placed row is the bound rounded down to 32 | Yes |
| Subsampling jobs; padded rows | None | 20; 8 | 20; 8 | Yes |
| Placement work per call | None | 2 loads, 1 compare | `adrp`, `ldr`, `cmp`, `b.hs`, `adrp`, `add`, `ldr`, `ret`: 2 loads, 1 compare | Yes |
| Copies per weight, code and sum byte | 1 weight expansion per call | 0, 0, 0 | The dispatcher copies nothing; the hook's copies need the GPU kernel's check | Pending |
| Subsampling codes written; lines cleaned | 7,032,960; 0 | 7,032,960; 219,780 (8.9 ms at 494 MHz) | 7,032,960; 219,780 (8.9 ms) | Yes |
| Recognizer wake-ups; IPIs; tick waits per job | None | 1; 0; 0 with INTID 95, else up to one 4 ms wait | Recognizer, worker and INTID 95 on one core; 204 × 4 ms = 0.82 s at most without INTID 95 | Pending the GPU runtime |
| Arena peak | 1,761,840 bytes | At most 2,784,048 bytes | Needs the mimus port's 224-row producer | Pending |
| mimus arena within the 12 MiB span | 16 MiB | At most 12 MiB, asserted at compile time | The assertion compiles with 12 MiB and fails with 16 MiB or a base moved by 4 KiB; `recorded.h` still declares 16 MiB | Pending the mimus port |
| GPU idle per subsampling gap | None | At most 1 ms on the A55 pair, 0.25 ms on the A76 pair | Clean of one block 0.449 ms and 0.111 ms; production time needs the mimus port | Pending |

**Jobs.** Every bench call fits one job under the worker's bound, so the
204 placed calls are 204 jobs. The C hook model and the Python time model
both count 204.

**Linear stage.** On the A55 pair the modeled 0.812 s is 0.579 s of GPU
compute, 0.157 s of read-out shared by both cores, 0.064 s of cache
maintenance (596,989 cleaned and 988,060 invalidated lines) and 0.012 s of
submit, wake and hand-off. With one job in flight nothing but the CPU
channels of a split call overlaps a job. On the A76 pair 0.366 s of GPU
compute for 62.9% of the MACs dominates the 0.414 s. The first bound of
0.79 s and 0.39 s assumed overlapped two-job calls; under that model the
best split points gave 0.813 s and 0.407 s, so no placement recovers it. No
regression against the CPU path exists.

**Table.** On the A55 pair every tensor is GPU-only. A channel split moves
read-out that both cores share in a GPU-only call onto the recognizer core:
the feed-forward first linear takes 6.25 ms GPU-only and 7.95 ms with
16 CPU channels.

Other host results:

| Item | Base | Current |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Resident image `.text` / `.rodata` / `.data` / `.bss` | 845,088 / 41,321 / 3,168 / 1,481,568 B | Same |
| Dispatcher object `apps/os/dispatch.c` for AArch64 `.text` / `.rodata` / `.bss` | None | 512 / 2,345 / 36 B, in the image only with the option |
| Translations in `mimus_board_pins` for the arena | 4,096 | 4,096 without the option; 5,120 with it |
| Read-only rule refusals: one writable, unreadable or Device page at the first, middle or last of 1,024 pages | None | All 9 cases refused |
| Job with a missing tag | None | The rest of the call and every later call on the CPU, exact sums, no `board_fail` |
| Supervision: reply never comes | None | Watchdog expiry 6.02 s after the wait begins, 4 s after the last renewal |
| Supervision: two jobs at the worker's deadline | None | Renewal continues |
| Longest input, 820 frames | None | 277 calls, 408 jobs on the A55 pair with up to 4 per call; 311 on the A76 pair with up to 3; no zero-row job and no job above the worker's bound |
| Configuration with the option | None | Refused without the resident lifetime or either constant; configures with both, with and without the microphone |
| Link check with the option | None | INTIDs 71 and 95, entries `mimus`, `thermal`, `gpu-linear`; refuses a recognition core of 6 with INTID 95 on core 2 |

Every count, the lookup cost, the job bound and the exact-sum comparison
meet their budgets. The modeled linear stage meets the restated regression
bound and misses the first one by 2.8% and 6.2%; the restated bound needs the
performance panel's acceptance. Against the 14.894 s CPU baseline on one A55
it is 18 and 36 times shorter. Default images are unchanged. Copies, the
arena peak, the subsampling gap and the wake-up counts need the GPU kernel,
the mimus port and the GPU runtime before they can be measured.
narrative:
Method.

- **Images.** The base commit was exported with `git archive` and both
  commits were configured with the shared configuration script and built with
  `-j 6` under `~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/recognition-dispatch/`. Four default
  OS variants were built at each commit: supervised, resident, resident with
  the I2S microphone and resident with the Bluetooth headset. A second,
  independent build of the supervised and resident variants under
  `~/.cache/sunstoneos/build/recognition-dispatch-measure/` gave the same
  sizes and the same result from the host check. `llvm-size-21
  -A` gave the section sizes and `llvm-objcopy-21 -O binary` the loadable
  bytes.
- **GPU option.** A resident build with `SUNSTONE_A733_OS_GPU_LINEAR`, both
  build constants and the bench models compiled every changed source for
  AArch64 except the patched recognizer, which stopped at its assertion that
  mimus's arena is at most 12 MiB: `apps/mimus/recorded.h` declares 16 MiB.
  With a copy of that header declaring 12 MiB placed in the build directory,
  the recognizer compiled and linking stopped at the five functions that other
  owners provide. Linking the same objects with empty definitions of those
  five functions gave an image for the link check only.
- **Dispatcher and time model.** `checks/os-image-dispatch.py` generated the
  A55-pair table at 494 MHz and the A76-pair table at 2,002 MHz from the bench
  models (`~/.cache/sunstoneos/inputs/mimus-bench`). It ran
  `checks/os-image-dispatch.c`, built with AddressSanitizer and
  UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, over the bench recording's call list
  (222 encoder frames) with exact integer sums, and over the longest accepted
  input (820 frames) with output coverage only. It disassembled
  `os_dispatch_place` for AArch64 and ran the CMake gate cases against the
  resident base build's cache.

The base commit has no placement path, so its rows below are the CPU-only

baseline.

Base commit c45a76e (audit/integration); kernel design commit f60d41c on branch audit/gpu-mimus-compute (docs/designs/gpu-mimus-compute.md). Bench recording: 8.87 s of audio, 222 encoder frames, 4.17 billion MACs; CPU baseline 14.894 s linear stage of 19.476 s on one Cortex-A55 at 494 MHz with NEON kernels.

hypothesis: Some lever or combination brings the modeled linear stage to the 0.15 s goal.
prediction:
**Time estimate.** `apps/os/placement.py` computes every figure below with
the seeds of "The placement table" and the GPU at 400 MHz
(`A733_GPU_INITIAL_HZ`), its only verified clock. On the A55 pair the linear
stage takes 0.812 s:

- GPU compute for 204 jobs, including firmware overhead, 0.579 s;
- read-out of 12,923,134 sums at 12 instructions each, shared by both cores,
  0.157 s;
- 596,989 cleaned lines and 988,060 invalidated lines, tags included, at
  20 cycles each, 0.064 s;
- submit, wake and hand-off, 60 µs per job, 0.012 s.

Nothing overlaps the GPU job except the CPU channels of a split call, so the
read-out and cache maintenance are exposed in full. The regression bound of
0.82 s and 0.42 s is this result rounded up to 10 ms. It replaces 0.79 s and
0.39 s, which assumed that a call split into two jobs whose read-out
overlapped and that the recognizer core read out without computing CPU
channels. With 32-row boundaries, a 222-row call splits into 96 and 126 rows,
and the recognizer core is one of the two CPU workers; the kernel design also
keeps one job in flight. No placement recovers the earlier bound: under the
two-job model, the best split points gave 0.813 s and 0.407 s.

Until INTID 95 is qualified, the timed wake can add up to 204 × 4 ms. The
other stages alone take 2.29 s on the A55 pair, so the A55 configuration
cannot meet the goal. The A76 pair at 2,002 MHz takes 0.414 s, with 0.366 s
of GPU compute for 62.9% of the MACs. The same model on the A76 pair gives
these figures for the remaining levers:

| Lever | Owner | Linear stage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| GPU at 600 or 800 MHz | GPU power and thermal owner | 0.332 s or 0.288 s |
| NEON int32-lane accumulation at 2×, 3× or 4× the CPU rate | mimus port | 0.302 s, 0.241 s or 0.195 s |
| Read-out of the GPU share on both cores in channel splits | Kernel design | 0.404 s |
| 800 MHz and 3× | Two owners | 0.197 s |
| 800 MHz and 4× | Two owners | 0.169 s |
| 800 MHz, 4× and read-out on both cores | All three | 0.163 s |

No row meets 0.15 s. At 800 MHz and 4× the GPU computes for 0.128 s of the
0.169 s, so the call is GPU-bound; the CPU channels run in parallel with the
job, and cache maintenance, read-out and per-job overhead take the remaining
0.041 s. The kernel design leaves out more jobs in flight, which would hide
part of that remainder, until the board measures job overhead. No GPU operating point above 400 MHz is recorded, and the CPU
factors are unmeasured.

Host cases in `checks/os-image-dispatch.c`:

- no OPEN before the hash;
- refusal, and RESET and LOST each ending in `board_fail` with no CPU row
  computed after the failed job;
- a worker that never answers OPEN, close or a job, which expires the window;
- two consecutive jobs near the worker's deadline that end OK;
- a job that reports OK with a missing tag, which moves the rest of the call
  and every later call to the CPU without ending the boot;
- no zero-row job, a bound below 32 rows giving `n_gpu = 0`, and the
  longest capture with three or more jobs per call;
- the emitted table for each core set and pair of clocks, every row's
  `job_rows` at most the worker's formula, and the modeled linear stage
  within the regression bound;
- the recognizer patch's arena assertion, which accepts a 12 MiB arena at
  `0x46000000` and refuses a 16 MiB arena or another base;
- configuration with the option on and the resident lifetime or either build
  constant missing, which fails.
conclusion: No lever combination meets 0.15 s; the best is 0.163 s on the A76 pair (800 MHz, 4x NEON accumulation and read-out on both cores). The A55 pair cannot meet the goal because its other stages alone take 2.29 s. Not measured on a board; no GPU operating point above 400 MHz was recorded then and the CPU factors are unmeasured.

hypothesis: Alternatives left out of the placement design cost less than they save, or are blocked by a stated condition.
prediction:
- **NPU placement.** The pinned NPU compiler refuses the INT32 output that
  exact sums need, and its input quantization uses one scale where mimus uses
  one per row ([npu-mimus-linear.md](../npu-mimus-linear.md)). It returns when
  exact sums build with the pinned compiler.
- **Recovery from RESET or LOST without a reboot.** It would keep GPU rows
  after RESET, or close the session, clean and invalidate the model regions
  and arena span, re-hash, reload the engine cold and recompute on the CPU.
  It returns when the board shows that a GPU write through a read-only
  mapping faults and leaves memory unchanged.
- **Read-out of the GPU share on both cores in channel splits.** The kernel
  design leaves it out. This model gives a saving of 10 ms on the A76 pair at
  2,002 MHz, where the kernel design's model gives 1.3 ms; the board's
  read-out rate settles which one holds.
- **A minimum row count per tensor.** Every placed tensor has K × N of at
  least 30,976, so a 32,768-MAC break-even needs at most two rows, and the
  smallest bench call has 30. A board-measured rate that makes it bind brings
  it back as a table column.
- **Gathering subsampling windows from unexpanded codes.** Each window has its
  own quantization scale, so windows cannot share codes without changing the
  output.
- **Overlapping subsampling production with GPU work.** It needs a second code
  buffer and an asynchronous hook, and returns if the board shows the 19 gaps
  above 20 ms in total.
- **One job for the query, key and value projections**, until board-measured
  job overhead shows that the engine change pays.
- **Thermal load shedding.** The image ignores THROTTLE; CRITICAL ends the
  session.
conclusion: Not measured; each item returns under its stated condition. Read-out of the GPU share on both cores saves 10 ms on the A76 pair at 2,002 MHz in this model (1.3 ms in the kernel design's); the board read-out rate settles which holds.

hypothesis: The board confirms the placement design: recognition equal to the host reference with every placed call on the GPU, a faulting EL0 store into the output view, INTID 95 on the recognition core, and failure injection ending in a watchdog reset.
prediction:
- The GPU build recognizes the bench recording with text and CRCs equal to the
  host, and the dispatch record shows every placed call on the GPU.
- An EL0 store into `0x46C00000`–`0x47000000` faults, and the check in
  `mimus_board_pins` passes.
- INTID 95 arrives on the recognition core for every job.
- An injected hang ends in RESET, `board_fail` and a watchdog reset; after it,
  and after an injected LOST, the loader's model hashes match. A one-hour
  resident run never stops watchdog renewal.
- CPU and GPU rates per shape at each admitted clock replace the table's
  seeds.
conclusion: Not yet run; the items are listed under open work of the design.
